site.title: My Claude Code: local LLM gateway for coding agents
site.description: A local multi-provider LLM proxy and router for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI: 60 providers, fallback routing, credential health and cost.

features.title: Features: every capability of the local LLM gateway
features.description: Routing and fallback, reasoning budgets, 60 providers with credential health, agent support, observability with cost provenance, web search and the dashboard.

features/routing.title: Model routing and fallback chains for coding agents
features/routing.description: Turn the model name an agent asks for into a real provider model, then walk an ordered chain of stand-ins when it cannot serve, with a logged reason per step.

features/reasoning-and-budgets.title: Reasoning control and output budgets per request
features/reasoning-and-budgets.description: Set reasoning effort and output budgets per model and per agent, and keep them across providers that spell the same control differently.

features/providers-and-credentials.title: 60 providers, keys and credential health
features/providers-and-credentials.description: Sixty providers behind one address, each with its own keys, rotation and credential health: see which key served a request and which needs rotating.

features/agents.title: Agent support: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI
features/agents.description: Launch the CLI agents, configure the desktop apps MCC cannot launch, generate a model catalogue for each, and name the agent behind every request.

features/observability-and-cost.title: Request log, analytics and cost with provenance
features/observability-and-cost.description: Every request logged with the model that served it, the tokens it used and what it cost, with provenance: which provider, key and price produced the number.

features/web-search.title: Native web search and fetch proxy for any model
features/web-search.description: Fulfil Claude Code's web_search and web_fetch at the proxy against a provider you choose or a keyless fallback: no Anthropic search credits, any model provider.

features/messaging.title: Messaging surfaces for the local gateway
features/messaging.description: The messaging surface MCC exposes beside the proxy, with the same routing, logging and cost accounting as every other request that passes through the gateway.

features/media.title: Media handling in the local LLM gateway
features/media.description: How MCC handles media requests and media tool responses through the same proxy path, with the same logging, routing and cost accounting as text requests.

features/platform.title: Platform support: Windows, macOS and Linux
features/platform.description: Where MCC runs, what the installer does on each platform, and what it deliberately does not touch: the supported platforms, verified from the build and CI.

features/cli.title: The MCC command line
features/cli.description: The command line that starts the gateway, manages providers and keys, checks credential health and prints the state of every configured agent.

features/dashboard.title: The local control-plane dashboard
features/dashboard.description: The dashboard that shows routing, providers, credentials, requests and cost in one place, running locally beside the gateway and reading the same request log.

quick-start.title: Quick start: install and run the LLM gateway
quick-start.description: Install MCC, point your first agent at it, add a provider key and see the first request in the log: the shortest path from nothing to a working local gateway.

architecture.title: Architecture: how the local LLM gateway works
architecture.description: The doors, the routing ladder, the credential layer, the request log and the cost model: the system map, and the lifecycle of one request from door to reply.

architecture/request-path.title: Request path: from a door to a committed reply
architecture/request-path.description: What happens between an agent sending a request and the reply being committed: the door, model resolution, the routing ladder, the provider call and the log.

architecture/provider-routing.title: Provider routing and the fallback ladder
architecture/provider-routing.description: How MCC resolves a model name to a provider model, orders the fallback ladder, and decides when to move to the next rung: verified against the code.

architecture/credential-health.title: Credential health and key rotation
architecture/credential-health.description: How keys are stored, checked, rotated and attributed to requests: the credential layer behind the providers page, and what happens when a key starts failing.

architecture/cost-provenance.title: Cost provenance: where every number comes from
architecture/cost-provenance.description: How MCC attributes a cost to a request: which provider, which key, which price and which token count produced it, and what it does when a price is unknown.

architecture/data-and-storage.title: Data and storage: what MCC keeps and where
architecture/data-and-storage.description: What the gateway writes to disk, where the request log and the configuration live, and what is never stored: the data layout at product level.
keywords: where claude code proxy stores data

architecture/security-model.title: Security model: keys, boundaries and local-first
architecture/security-model.description: The security principles of a local gateway: keys stay on the machine, requests go only where you point them, and the boundary between agent and provider.

configuration.title: Configuration: how MCC settings are provided
configuration.description: Where MCC reads its settings, which ones apply per agent and which per provider, and how a change takes effect without restarting every client.

configuration/environment.title: Environment variables and settings reference
configuration/environment.description: Every environment variable MCC reads, what each one controls, whether it is required, and where in the code it is read: names and purposes, never values.

gallery.title: Gallery: the MCC dashboard and screens
gallery.description: The real screens of the local gateway: routing, providers, credentials, the request log, cost analytics and the agent pages, captured from the running product.

glossary.title: Glossary of gateway and routing terms
glossary.description: Door, tier, rung, ladder, credential health, cost provenance: every term MCC uses, defined once, with the behaviour it names.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about the gateway
faq.description: Answers to the questions people actually ask about MCC: which providers work, what happens when a key fails, where data is stored, and what it does not do.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting the local gateway
troubleshooting.description: Verified fixes for the problems people hit: a provider that will not answer, a key that stopped working, a request never logged, an agent that cannot connect.

about.title: About My Claude Code
about.description: Who builds MCC, what state the project is in, how it is built and what it is not: an independent local-first project, not affiliated with Anthropic.

license.title: Licence: AGPL and the commercial option
license.description: The AGPL-3.0 licence MCC ships under, the commercial option beside it, the third-party attributions, and the non-affiliation notice for Anthropic.

404.html.title: Page not found | My Claude Code
404.html.description: That address is not on this site. The front door links to every capability, the architecture and the gallery, so start there and follow the route you meant.

for/claude-code.title: Claude Code through a local LLM proxy
for/claude-code.description: Point Claude Code at My Claude Code with mcc-claude: one address, your own providers and keys, fallback chains, reasoning control and a priced request log.

for/codex.title: Codex CLI through a local LLM proxy
for/codex.description: Point Codex CLI at My Claude Code with mcc-codex over the OpenAI Responses API, with one provider set, fallback chains and a priced request log behind it.

for/opencode.title: OpenCode through a local LLM proxy
for/opencode.description: Point OpenCode at My Claude Code with mcc-opencode: an MCC-owned config file, your own providers, keys and fallback chains, and a priced request log.

for/gemini-cli.title: Gemini CLI through a local LLM proxy
for/gemini-cli.description: Point Gemini CLI at My Claude Code with mcc-gemini over the Gemini API surface, with one provider set, fallback chains and a priced request log behind it.
